One thousand borrowers can still be concentrated if most depend on the same property market or commodity price. ### Flow ### Where it sits ### Ownership | Role | Responsibility | | :--- | :--- | | Produces | Risk data and portfolio teams aggregate exposures and common drivers | | Approves | Board/senior risk governance sets appetite and concentration limits | | Consumes | Underwriting, limits, strategy, stress testing and capital planning | | Challenges | Independent risk and audit test aggregation, taxonomy and limit exceptions | ### Permanent rule Diversification must be judged by independence of loss drivers, not by nominal borrower count. ### Never confuse [Concentration] and [Large exposure] **Concentration** — dependence on a common source of loss, which may be name, sector, geography, collateral or another factor. --- **Large exposure** — an exposure or connected-group exposure meeting a defined regulatory or internal size threshold; concentration is broader. ### Permanent trap Splitting one economic group across subsidiaries or one common sector across narrow industry codes can improve a report while leaving the underlying loss concentration unchanged. ### Jurisdiction variants #### IN (RBI) RBI’s Large Exposures Framework governs prudential single-counterparty and connected-counterparty aggregation and limits. Internal concentration management must still capture sector and common-factor risks outside the legal large-exposure perimeter. #### UK (PRA) PRA large-exposure rules and SS3/25 govern connected-client identification; concentration risk also feeds broader supervisory and Pillar 2 assessment. #### EU CRR large-exposure rules constrain single clients and groups of connected clients; broader concentration risk remains a risk-management and supervisory concern. #### US US legal lending limits use US-specific aggregation rules. Internal sector and factor concentration management is broader than statutory single-borrower limits.

title: Correlation and systematic credit risk
one_screen: Credit correlation means default and loss outcomes are not independent because common economic forces move many borrowers together. Idiosyncratic risk can be diversified across sufficiently independent exposures; systematic risk cannot be removed by adding more borrowers exposed to the same underlying conditions.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Risk source | Example | Diversification effect | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Idiosyncratic | Fraud, plant failure, loss of one customer | Falls as many independent names are added | | Sector systematic | Commodity-price collapse, industry disruption | Persists across borrowers in the same sector | | Macro systematic | Recession, unemployment, rate shock | Can affect many sectors and borrowers together | | Recovery dependence | Property prices fall during mortgage defaults | Defaults and LGDs can worsen together | | Utilisation dependence | Revolvers draw in stress | Defaults and EAD can worsen together | Correlation does not require equal PDs. A 1% PD firm and a 5% PD firm can still become riskier at the same time because both respond to recession, rates or a common customer base. ### Flow ### Where it sits ### Formula ### Permanent rule Adding exposures diversifies risk only to the extent that their failure drivers are not the same. ### Never confuse [Correlation] and [Concentration] **Correlation** — dependence between credit outcomes. --- **Concentration** — disproportionate exposure to names or common drivers; concentration magnifies the consequence of dependence but is not the same concept. ### Permanent trap Assuming legal independence implies default independence systematically understates loss clustering during common economic stress. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** Correlation and systematic risk are economic and statistical properties; prudential frameworks differ in how dependence is parameterised, stressed or capitalised.

title: Unexpected loss and capital
one_screen: Expected loss is the average credit cost under a defined measurement; unexpected loss is adverse variation around that average. Capital protects solvency against sufficiently severe outcomes above ordinary expected-loss capacity, so portfolio dispersion and dependence matter even when exposure-level EL is unchanged.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Layer | Question | Main drivers | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Expected loss | What loss is anticipated on average? | PD, LGD, EAD and their aligned conditioning | | Loss volatility | How much can realised loss vary? | Granularity, parameter variation, migration | | Tail / unexpected loss | How severe can adverse loss become above the mean? | Concentration, correlation, systematic stress | | Capital | What loss-absorbing resources protect solvency? | Prudential/economic confidence standard and capital rules | Two portfolios can have identical EL but very different tail risk. One may contain thousands of diversified exposures; another may depend on a few correlated names. Their average loss can match while their severe-loss quantiles do not. ### Flow ### Where it sits ### Formula ### Permanent rule Expected loss and capital answer different questions: average credit cost versus protection against adverse loss beyond that average. ### Never confuse [Expected loss] and [Capital] **Expected loss** — probability-weighted average credit loss for the defined measurement. --- **Capital** — loss-absorbing resources held under a regulatory or internal solvency framework; it is not simply `PD × LGD × EAD`. ### Permanent trap Calling exposure-level EL “capital” ignores diversification, correlation, concentration and the shape of the portfolio loss distribution. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta in the conceptual split.** Regulatory capital formulas, buffers, Pillar 2 practices and accounting/provision regimes vary materially across jurisdictions.

title: The credit-loss architecture
one_screen: Credit risk is one continuous system: identify the person and exposure, decide whether repayment is sustainable, recognise default consistently, measure probability, severity and exposure, then aggregate common loss drivers into portfolio tail risk. The architecture fails when adjacent layers are collapsed—for example, collateral into repayment capacity, DPD into default, score into PD, or expected loss into capital.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Layer | Owns the question | Core objects | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Credit object | Who owes what? | Obligor · Facility · Account · Exposure · Connected group | | Credit decision | Should this risk be taken and on what terms? | Policy · Repayment capacity · Approval · Mitigants | | Credit state | Has contractual credit performance failed under the governed rule? | DPD · UTP · Default · Restructuring · Cure · Write-off | | Risk parameters | How likely, how severe, how much exposed? | PD · LGD · EAD | | Expected loss | What is the average loss cost? | PD × LGD × EAD under aligned definitions | | Risk measurement system | How is risk ranked and observed through time? | Retail pools · Scores · Bureau data · Ratings · Migration · Vintages | | Portfolio tail | What can fail together? | Concentration · Correlation · Systematic risk | | Solvency protection | What absorbs severe loss above the mean? | Unexpected loss · Capital | ### Flow ### Where it sits ### Permanent rule Keep each layer’s question separate, then connect the outputs deliberately. A precise answer at the wrong layer is still the wrong risk measure. ### Never confuse [Expected loss capacity] and [Capital] **Expected loss capacity** — pricing, provisions/allowances or other mechanisms that recognise and absorb anticipated credit cost under the applicable framework. --- **Capital** — resources protecting solvency against adverse outcomes beyond ordinary expected loss, under the applicable capital regime. ### Permanent trap A credit pack becomes incoherent when the same label is used for several layers—for example “risk” meaning score, PD, EL, provision and capital depending on the page. Always name the object, state and measure. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** The architecture is universal. Jurisdictions differ in prudential definitions, accounting treatment, regulatory formulas, thresholds and legal enforceability, but those variants sit inside the same object → state → parameter → portfolio-loss chain.

title: Risk Data as an Enterprise Discipline
one_screen: Risk data management is the discipline of making risk information reliable enough to steer a bank, not merely storing data or producing reports. It connects governed source data to aggregation, decisions, internal risk reporting and supervisory reporting, with evidence that the chain can still work under stress.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism A risk-data framework therefore controls four linked questions: | Question | Control objective | | :--- | :--- | | What does the datum mean? | Common definition, metadata and glossary | | Where did it come from? | Authoritative source and lineage | | Can it be relied on? | Data quality rules, reconciliation and issue management | | Who is accountable? | Owner, steward, producer, consumer and challenge roles | Risk measures themselves remain owned elsewhere: PD, LGD, EAD and RWA are credit and capital concepts; ECL staging is impairment; LCR and NSFR are liquidity. DAT owns the enterprise data chain that carries such measures into decisions and reporting. ### Where it sits ### Ownership | Role | Core accountability | | :--- | :--- | | Producer | Creates or transforms data | | Data owner | Accountable for governed meaning and fitness for use | | Data steward | Operates standards, monitoring and remediation | | Consumer | Uses data and identifies fitness-for-use failures | | Challenge | Independently tests whether controls and evidence deserve reliance | ### Permanent rule A report cannot be more trustworthy than the data, definitions, controls and accountability that produced it. ### Permanent trap Treating risk data as an IT problem because systems store it. Technology operates the plumbing; business accountability determines meaning, materiality and acceptable quality. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** The enterprise mechanics do not change by jurisdiction; local regulators differ mainly in reporting requirements and supervisory enforcement.

title: BCBS 239: The Fourteen-Principle Architecture
one_screen: BCBS 239 is the Basel Committee's data aggregation and internal risk reporting standard, not a capital calculation rule. Its fourteen principles form one chain: governance and infrastructure enable reliable aggregation; reliable aggregation enables useful reporting; supervisors assess whether the whole capability works.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Group | Principles | What the group owns | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Governance and infrastructure | 1-2 | Governance; data architecture and IT infrastructure | | Risk data aggregation capabilities | 3-6 | Accuracy and integrity; completeness; timeliness; adaptability | | Risk reporting practices | 7-11 | Accuracy; comprehensiveness; clarity and usefulness; frequency; distribution | | Supervisory review, tools and cooperation | 12-14 | Review; remedial action and supervisory measures; home-host cooperation | The standard was issued after the financial crisis exposed banks that could not identify group-wide exposures and concentrations fully, quickly and accurately. It initially targeted global systemically important banks, while supervisors and banks have since used its principles more broadly as a benchmark for risk-data governance. ### Where it sits ### Never confuse [BCBS 239] and [Basel capital rules] **BCBS 239** - sets principles for risk data aggregation and internal risk reporting capabilities. --- **Basel capital rules** - determine prudential capital requirements and related calculations; DAT does not re-teach those mechanics. ### Permanent rule The fourteen principles are not fourteen independent checklist items. Weakness in governance or architecture propagates into aggregation and then into reporting. ### Permanent trap Reducing BCBS 239 to a data-quality programme. Data quality is essential, but the standard also owns governance, architecture, adaptability, report usefulness, distribution and supervisory remediation. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** The BCBS principles themselves do not change by jurisdiction; their legal and supervisory implementation can.

title: BCBS 239 Governance and Data Architecture
one_screen: BCBS 239 Principles 1-2 make risk data a management-body and enterprise-architecture responsibility. The bank must be able to aggregate and report material risk information despite legal-entity complexity, organisational change, stress, acquisitions or fragmented technology.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Principle | Required capability | Evidence in practice | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | 1 Governance | Senior management and the board oversee risk data aggregation and reporting within the risk-management framework | Policy, scope, accountability, resources, independent review, issue escalation | | 2 Data architecture and IT infrastructure | Architecture supports accurate, complete and timely aggregation in normal and stressed conditions | Documented architecture, integrated taxonomies, controlled interfaces, resilience, change impact assessment | A merger, new product or system replacement is therefore a risk-data event, not just a technology event. If the change creates a new source, mapping, identifier or legal-entity boundary, the reporting chain must absorb it without losing traceability. ### Where it sits ### Ownership | Role | Governance consequence | | :--- | :--- | | Board and senior management | Set direction, approve framework, demand remediation | | Business data owners | Account for meaning and fitness of governed data | | IT and data engineering | Build and operate architecture to approved requirements | | Independent challenge | Tests design, implementation and evidence | ### Permanent rule Architecture choices cannot be allowed to make material risk unknowable at the level where management or supervisors need it. ### Permanent trap Treating a successful nightly load as proof of architecture adequacy. Principle 2 is about the end-to-end ability to aggregate under changing and stressed conditions, not batch completion alone. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** The principles are universal; local supervisors may impose different remediation mechanisms or additional expectations.

title: BCBS 239 Risk Data Aggregation Capabilities
one_screen: BCBS 239 Principles 3-6 define what a bank's aggregation engine must achieve: accurate and integral data, complete coverage, decision-useful timeliness and adaptability to new questions. The standard is outcomes-based; it does not create a universal 95 percent completeness threshold or a universal daily or intraday frequency.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Principle | Question it answers | Failure example | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | 3 Accuracy and integrity | Are values produced reliably, with controlled manual intervention and appropriate reconciliation? | Unexplained spreadsheet adjustments change exposure totals | | 4 Completeness | Are all material risks, entities, business lines and relevant dimensions captured? | A subsidiary or product is outside aggregation scope | | 5 Timeliness | Is information available quickly enough for the risk and decision being managed? | Stress exposure arrives after the decision window | | 6 Adaptability | Can the bank answer new or ad-hoc risk questions without rebuilding the data estate? | A supervisor asks for sector-by-country exposure and the bank cannot produce it promptly | Timeliness is contextual: a slowly changing structural metric and a fast-moving trading exposure can require different refresh speeds. Adaptability is likewise not limitless flexibility; the point is that common risk dimensions and detailed data are governed well enough to support credible new views. ### Where it sits ### Never confuse [Completeness] and [Accuracy] **Completeness** - the required material population and dimensions are present. --- **Accuracy** - the values and transformations correctly represent the governed source and intended measure. A complete dataset can still be wrong. ### Permanent rule Aggregation quality is fit-for-purpose across all four capabilities; excellence in one dimension does not cancel failure in another. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** The aggregation principles do not change by jurisdiction.

title: BCBS 239 Risk Reporting Practices
one_screen: BCBS 239 Principles 7-11 govern the report after aggregation: it must faithfully represent risk, cover the material picture, communicate it clearly, arrive at the right frequency and reach the right recipients. A technically correct dataset can still fail BCBS 239 if the report obscures the decision, omits relevant context or is distributed too late.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Principle | Reporting test | | :--- | :--- | | 7 Accuracy | Report outputs faithfully represent aggregated risk data and are reconciled or otherwise controlled | | 8 Comprehensiveness | Material risks, concentrations and relevant forward-looking information are covered at suitable depth | | 9 Clarity and usefulness | Content is concise enough to support action, while definitions, limits, trends and exceptions are intelligible | | 10 Frequency | Production frequency matches the volatility of risk and recipient decision needs, including stress | | 11 Distribution | Reports reach authorised recipients through controlled channels with confidentiality preserved | Clarity is not cosmetic simplification. A board report may aggregate heavily, but it must preserve the information needed to identify concentrations, limit breaches and emerging risk. A desk-level report may be more granular because the consumer needs operational detail. ### Where it sits ### Never confuse [Data timeliness] and [Report frequency] **Data timeliness** - how quickly current data can be aggregated for the decision need. --- **Report frequency** - how often a defined report is produced and distributed. A monthly report can depend on data that must still be available rapidly for ad-hoc stress analysis. ### Permanent trap Equating more pages with comprehensiveness. A report can be large yet fail to expose the risk, exception or concentration that the recipient needs to act on. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** The reporting-practice principles are universal; local return formats are covered later.

title: BCBS 239 Supervisory Review and Implementation Record
one_screen: BCBS 239 does not end when a bank writes a policy: Principles 12-14 require supervisors to assess implementation, demand remediation and cooperate across home and host authorities. The implementation record remains active; a Basel Committee newsletter dated 6 January 2026 describes persistent challenges and expressly states that it creates no new supervisory guidance or expectations.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Principle | Supervisory function | | :--- | :--- | | 12 Review | Supervisors periodically assess compliance with the principles | | 13 Remedial actions and supervisory measures | Deficiencies require timely remediation; supervisors can use available tools where progress is inadequate | | 14 Home-host cooperation | Supervisors cooperate across jurisdictions for cross-border banking groups | The 2026 Basel newsletter identifies recurring themes including governance, lineage, cross-border implementation, changing operating environments, emerging technology and compensating controls. It describes implementation as continuous because mergers, new products, technology and risk landscapes keep changing the aggregation problem. ### Where it sits ### Permanent rule BCBS 239 compliance is a sustained capability, not a one-time programme closure date. ### Permanent trap Treating a compensating control as evidence that the underlying defect is solved. A manual or detective control can contain risk while structural remediation remains open. ### Jurisdiction variants #### EU (ECB Banking Supervision) The ECB's May 2024 RDARR Guide clarifies supervisory expectations for significant institutions and is used in targeted reviews and remediation monitoring; it does not replace BCBS 239. #### UK (PRA) The PRA applies its supervisory toolkit through the UK prudential framework; this atom does not invent a separate UK version of the fourteen principles. #### US US agencies use their own supervisory processes and reporting expectations; the Basel principles remain a benchmark rather than a US form specification. #### IN (RBI) RBI's 31 July 2026 Commercial Banks - Supervisory Returns Directions contain explicit governance, architecture, reconciliation and automation requirements for commercial-bank supervisory reporting.

title: Golden Source and Authoritative Data
one_screen: A golden source is the governed authority for a defined data element or dataset, not simply the database with the newest copy. Authority means the bank has decided which source wins, for what scope and time, with ownership, controls and explicit treatment of downstream copies and exceptions.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Decision | Golden-source question | | :--- | :--- | | Scope | Which data element, entity, product or population does this authority cover? | | Authority | Which system or controlled record is the official source? | | Timing | At what event time, effective date or reporting cut-off is it authoritative? | | Control | How are updates, corrections and overrides governed? | | Consumption | Which downstream processes must source from it or reconcile to it? | A bank can legitimately have different authoritative sources for different concepts: customer legal name, product classification, accounting balance and risk exposure may each belong to different controlled domains. The rule is not one database for the bank; it is one governed authority per defined purpose and scope. ### Where it sits ### Never confuse [Golden source] and [Data warehouse] **Golden source** - the governed authority for a defined datum or population. --- **Data warehouse** - a repository that may contain integrated copies from many sources. It becomes authoritative only where governance explicitly assigns that role. ### Permanent rule When two systems disagree, governance must determine which source is authoritative and why; report teams must not choose whichever value makes the reconciliation easier. ### Permanent trap Using the phrase "single source of truth" without defining scope. Different data domains can have different authoritative sources without violating the golden-source principle. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** The concept is an enterprise data-governance mechanism, not a jurisdiction-specific return rule.

title: Critical Data Elements
one_screen: Critical Data Elements, or CDEs, are data elements whose failure could materially impair risk management, financial or supervisory reporting, customer or business decisions, or regulatory compliance. CDE designation is a scoping mechanism: it concentrates stronger ownership, lineage, quality and change controls where failure matters most.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | CDE test | Question | | :--- | :--- | | Regulatory dependency | Does the element directly determine a required reported value or classification? | | Risk-management dependency | Could an error distort exposure, concentration, limit or risk decision? | | Aggregation dependency | Is it a key identifier, amount, date or classification needed to consolidate correctly? | | Propagation | Would one defect contaminate many reports or downstream calculations? | | Recovery difficulty | Would late discovery make correction costly or impossible before a decision or filing? | A CDE is normally a governed field or business concept, not an entire database. "Counterparty identifier" may be critical because it drives legal-entity aggregation; every technical audit column in the same table need not become a CDE. ### Where it sits ### Ownership | Role | CDE responsibility | | :--- | :--- | | Owner | Approves meaning, scope and required quality | | Steward | Maintains metadata, controls and issue follow-up | | Producer | Supplies the element through the governed process | | Consumer | Confirms fitness for the material use | | Challenge | Tests whether designation and controls are credible | ### Permanent rule Criticality follows impact, not technical convenience or the number of reports containing the field. ### Permanent trap Declaring every field critical. If everything receives the same control intensity, criticality no longer helps prioritise scarce remediation and monitoring capacity. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** Regulators may use different terminology, but materiality-based scoping is not a country-specific mechanic.

title: Data Owner, Steward, Producer, Consumer and Challenge
one_screen: Risk data governance fails when accountability is collapsed into one vague "data team". The owner, steward, producer, consumer and challenge function answer different questions: who is accountable for meaning and fitness, who operates governance, who creates or transforms the data, who relies on it, and who independently tests the evidence.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Role | Produces | Approves / decides | Consumes | Challenges | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Data owner | Business decisions on the data domain | Definition, required quality, priorities and risk acceptance | Quality and issue information | Producer and steward performance | | Data steward | Metadata, monitoring and remediation coordination | Operational changes within delegated authority | DQ results and issue evidence | Day-to-day adherence to standards | | Producer | Source or transformed data | Operational production controls | Requirements and mappings | Upstream defects and unclear requirements | | Consumer | Use-specific outputs and feedback | Acceptance for intended use where assigned | Data, reports and extracts | Fitness for purpose and unexplained changes | | Independent challenge | Review evidence and findings | Independent assessment, not business ownership | Policies, lineage, tests and issue records | Design and operating effectiveness | The same person may wear more than one role in a small organisation, but decision rights must remain explicit and incompatible duties should not become self-approval. ### Where it sits ### Never confuse [Data owner] and [Data steward] **Data owner** - accountable business authority for the governed data domain, including definition, required quality and prioritisation. --- **Data steward** - operational custodian of standards, metadata, monitoring and remediation coordination; stewardship does not remove the owner's accountability. ### Permanent trap Assigning "IT" as owner merely because IT hosts the system. System operation does not confer business authority to decide what exposure, customer, product or risk classification means. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** Organisational titles vary, but the separation of accountability, operation, production, use and independent challenge is a general governance need.

title: Data Governance Operating Models
one_screen: A data governance operating model turns roles into decision rights, forums, escalation paths and repeatable processes. Centralised, federated and hybrid models are organisational choices; none works if ownership is unclear or enterprise standards can be bypassed without controlled exception.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Model | Enterprise centre | Domain or business units | Main strength | Main failure mode | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Centralised | Makes most data decisions and operates standards | Execute centrally set decisions | Consistency | Bottleneck and weak business ownership | | Federated | Sets minimum policy and coordination | Make substantial domain decisions | Domain expertise and speed | Conflicting definitions and duplicated controls | | Hybrid | Owns enterprise standards, architecture and escalation | Own definitions, quality and delivery within standards | Balance of consistency and accountability | Ambiguous decision boundary | A workable model assigns each decision before a dispute occurs: Committees are mechanisms, not ownership. A data council can resolve cross-domain conflicts, but the committee should not become a place where accountability is diffused among attendees. ### Where it sits ### Ownership | Layer | Typical decision | | :--- | :--- | | Board / senior management | Framework, risk appetite, material remediation priorities | | Enterprise data governance | Common policy, taxonomy, architecture principles, cross-domain conflicts | | Domain owner | Definitions, quality requirements, local priorities and exceptions | | Stewardship | Metadata, monitoring, issue coordination and evidence | | Independent challenge | Whether design and operation are effective | ### Permanent rule A governance model is complete only when a person can determine who decides, who executes, who must be consulted and where unresolved conflict escalates. ### Permanent trap Measuring governance maturity by committee count. More forums can increase delay while leaving the actual decision right undefined. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** Regulators expect effective governance but do not impose one universal organisational design.

title: Business Lineage vs Technical Lineage
one_screen: Data lineage explains how a data item moves from origin to use and what happens to it on the way. Business lineage preserves meaning and dependency at a level a risk or reporting user can challenge; technical lineage preserves the physical systems, fields, transformations and interfaces needed to reproduce and troubleshoot the result.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Dimension | Business lineage | Technical lineage | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Starts from | Business concept or reporting item | Physical field, table, file, message or API | | Shows | Source concept, key transformations, aggregation and use | System hops, joins, filters, code logic and target fields | | Main users | Owners, consumers, risk, finance, audit, supervisors | Engineers, analysts, testers, control teams | | Main question | "What feeds this number and why?" | "Exactly where and how was this value produced?" | Good lineage links the two views. A business definition without technical traceability cannot prove implementation; technical pipes without business meaning cannot prove that the right concept was implemented. ### Where it sits ### Never confuse [Lineage] and [Source-to-target mapping] **Lineage** - the end-to-end dependency chain across sources, transformations and uses, often spanning several systems and mappings. --- **Source-to-target mapping** - the implementation specification for a defined source-to-target transformation. It can be an important component of lineage without being the whole lineage. ### Permanent rule For material risk data, a consumer should be able to move from reported value to business meaning and from that meaning down to the physical source and transformation evidence. ### Permanent trap Calling a system list "lineage". "Core banking -> warehouse -> report" identifies locations but not fields, transformations, dependencies or governed business meaning. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** Lineage mechanics are not jurisdiction-specific; supervisory depth of scrutiny can vary.

title: Metadata and the Business Glossary
one_screen: Metadata makes data interpretable and governable; a business glossary makes important business terms mean the same thing across functions and systems. Together they connect a human concept such as "counterparty exposure" to the fields, formats, owners, sources and lineage through which that concept is implemented.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Layer | Typical contents | Governance purpose | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Business glossary | Term, definition, scope, exclusions, owner, effective date | One governed business meaning | | Business metadata | CDE status, sensitivity, quality requirement, source authority, consumer | Control and accountability context | | Technical metadata | Field name, datatype, length, table, interface, code set, refresh | Precise implementation context | | Operational metadata | Load time, record count, control result, version | Evidence that the process ran as expected | Definitions need version control. If "defaulted exposure" changes meaning because policy or regulation changes, the bank needs the old and new definitions, effective dates, impacted reports and corresponding technical changes rather than silently overwriting the glossary entry. ### Where it sits ### Never confuse [Business glossary] and [Data dictionary] **Business glossary** - governed business language: what a term means and where its scope begins and ends. --- **Data dictionary** - field-level description of how data is represented technically. In this pack, dictionary detail is carried through metadata and mapping rather than a separate atom. ### Permanent rule A field name is not a definition. Meaning must be explicit enough that two independent teams would classify the same case the same way. ### Permanent trap Publishing a glossary without ownership or effective dates. A dictionary of prose that nobody is accountable for does not control semantic change. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** Common definitions and metadata are enterprise controls; jurisdiction-specific definitions enter through the governed terms, not through different metadata mechanics.

title: Master Data vs Reference Data
one_screen: Master data identifies and describes persistent business entities such as customers, counterparties, products or legal entities; reference data provides controlled code sets and classifications used to describe or group those entities and transactions. Both are shared across processes, but they solve different data problems and require different change controls.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Dimension | Master data | Reference data | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Represents | Core business entity | Permitted classification or code set | | Example | Counterparty record, product record, legal entity | Currency code, country code, sector code, rating scale | | Typical key problem | Duplicate or mismatched identity | Invalid, stale or inconsistent classification | | Change pattern | Entity created, merged, amended or retired | Code added, mapped, versioned or withdrawn | | Risk impact | Exposure split across duplicate identities | Exposure grouped into wrong category | The two interact. A counterparty master record may carry a country code from a controlled reference set; an exposure can be correctly linked to the customer yet still be misreported by geography if the reference code is wrong. ### Where it sits ### Never confuse [Master data] and [Reference data] **Master data** - governed records for the core entities with which the bank does business or about which it reports. --- **Reference data** - governed lists and codes used to classify, validate or interpret other data. ### Permanent rule Shared identifiers and classifications must be governed consistently across the reporting chain; local copies require controlled synchronisation or reconciliation. ### Permanent trap Fixing an aggregation problem only in the report. If the root cause is duplicate customer master data or a stale classification code, a report-level override leaves other consumers wrong. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** Jurisdictions can prescribe different classifications or reporting codes, but the distinction between master and reference data does not change.

title: Data Quality Dimensions
one_screen: Data quality is not one score. A dataset can be complete but inaccurate, valid but stale, or internally consistent while duplicating the same customer twice; quality must therefore be assessed across distinct dimensions against the needs of the specific risk or reporting use.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Dimension | Test | Example failure | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Accuracy | Does the value correctly represent the governed source or real-world fact? | Outstanding balance differs from authoritative record | | Completeness | Is the required population and required fields present? | One legal entity is absent from the exposure feed | | Consistency | Do equivalent concepts agree across systems or reports after allowed differences? | Same customer has conflicting sector classifications | | Timeliness | Is the data current and available when needed? | Position is accurate for yesterday but used for an intraday stress decision | | Validity | Does the value conform to defined type, range, format or code rules? | Country code is outside the approved list | | Uniqueness | Is each entity or event represented without unintended duplication? | One trade loaded twice | Quality is always tied to use. A reporting field can require exact validity but allow a documented timing tolerance; another field can require near-real-time availability because the risk changes rapidly. ### Where it sits ### Never confuse [Accuracy] and [Consistency] **Accuracy** - the value is correct against the governed fact or authoritative source. --- **Consistency** - equivalent representations agree after legitimate scope, timing and accounting differences are understood. Two systems can be consistently wrong. ### Permanent rule Quality is fit for purpose: the required dimensions and tolerances follow material use, not a universal enterprise score applied blindly to every datum. ### Permanent trap Reporting a high overall DQ percentage that averages away a critical failure. A small number of wrong CDEs can matter more than millions of clean low-impact fields. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** Quality dimensions do not change by regulator; return-specific tolerances and validation rules can.

title: Data Quality Rules, Thresholds and Monitoring
one_screen: A data-quality dimension becomes operational only when it is converted into a rule that can be executed, measured and escalated. A complete rule defines its population, condition, expected result, tolerance, ownership and breach action; a threshold without those elements is merely a number.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Rule component | Example | | :--- | :--- | | Population | All active corporate-loan records at reporting cut-off | | Dimension | Completeness | | Condition | Counterparty identifier is populated | | Expected result | Every in-scope record carries an approved identifier | | Threshold / tolerance | Governed level based on materiality and use | | Evidence | Exception population, pass rate, run timestamp, rule version | | Action | Investigate breach, assess report impact, remediate and escalate | Thresholds are risk decisions. Zero tolerance may be appropriate for a mandatory identifier in a small critical population; a different control may allow a documented tolerance where errors are immaterial and separately contained. The bank should not invent a Basel percentage and label it universal. ### Where it sits ### Ownership | Role | Contribution | | :--- | :--- | | Owner | Approves required quality and tolerance | | Steward | Maintains rule inventory and monitors results | | Producer | Fixes production causes within its process | | Consumer | Assesses use and reporting impact | | Challenge | Tests rule design, coverage and evidence | ### Permanent rule A quality metric without a defined population and governed threshold cannot support a defensible control conclusion. ### Permanent trap Tuning thresholds until dashboards turn green. Tolerances should reflect risk appetite and use, not the current defect rate. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** The control mechanic is universal; regulators or return taxonomies may impose specific validation rules for particular submissions.

title: Reconciliation and Break Governance
one_screen: Reconciliation compares two governed populations or totals that should agree after known differences are understood. Its value is not the act of matching numbers; it is the disciplined classification, ownership, ageing and clearance of breaks so unexplained differences cannot quietly enter risk reports or returns.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Reconciliation | Typical comparison | What it can reveal | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Front-to-back | Trading or origination records vs operations/accounting records | Missing, duplicated or mismapped transactions | | Risk-to-finance | Risk exposure or position totals vs finance/accounting totals | Scope, valuation, timing or transformation differences | | Source-to-report | Authoritative source population vs reporting extract | ETL, mapping, filter or aggregation defects | | Period-on-period | Current return vs prior period with explained movement | Unexpected discontinuity or reporting drift | A difference is not automatically an error. Accounting and risk views can legitimately use different scope or measurement; the control requirement is that differences are defined, quantified and explainable. ### Where it sits ### Never confuse [Reconciliation break] and [Data error] **Reconciliation break** - an observed difference between populations that requires explanation. --- **Data error** - a confirmed defect. Some breaks are expected timing, scope or measurement differences and should be evidenced rather than "fixed". ### Permanent rule A reconciliation is complete only when material breaks are explained, owned and dispositioned, not when the comparison file has run. ### Permanent trap Netting breaks to zero. Equal and opposite errors can make totals agree while individual records remain wrong. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** Reconciliation mechanics are universal; particular returns may prescribe additional validations.

title: Data Issue Management and Remediation
one_screen: A data issue is not closed when the immediate report is patched. Controlled remediation separates containment from permanent correction, identifies the root cause, assigns accountable ownership, validates the fix and retains evidence that the defect no longer recurs or remains within an explicitly accepted risk position.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Issue record must answer | Why it matters | | :--- | :--- | | What data and reports are affected? | Defines impact and consumers | | Since when? | Determines historical exposure and possible restatement | | What is the root cause? | Prevents cosmetic fixes | | What containment exists? | Controls current risk while remediation is open | | Who is accountable and by when? | Creates enforceable ownership | | What proves closure? | Stops tickets closing on assertion alone | Root causes can sit at source capture, master/reference data, definition, interface, transformation, manual adjustment or governance. The issue should be assigned to the party able to remove the cause, while the data owner remains accountable for the risk to the governed domain. ### Where it sits ### Never confuse [Workaround] and [Remediation] **Workaround** - temporary control or manual action that contains immediate impact while the defect remains. --- **Remediation** - change that removes or durably controls the root cause and is validated before closure. ### Permanent rule Closure evidence must demonstrate the root cause is resolved or that any residual risk is explicitly accepted through the proper governance route. ### Permanent trap Measuring success by ticket closure rate. Fast closure can conceal recurring issues if fixes address symptoms rather than sources. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** Supervisory escalation mechanisms vary, but sound issue lifecycle mechanics do not.

title: Data Requirements and Acceptance Criteria
one_screen: A data requirement converts a regulatory, risk or business need into a statement precise enough to source, build and test. For a business analyst, the critical move is from "produce this field" to governed meaning, grain, population, timing, transformation, control and acceptance criteria that different teams can implement consistently.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Requirement dimension | Question to resolve | | :--- | :--- | | Business meaning | What exactly does the item represent, including inclusions and exclusions? | | Grain | One row per what: account, facility, trade, customer, legal entity or aggregate? | | Population | Which products, entities, statuses, dates and geographies are in scope? | | Source intent | What type of authoritative information is required? | | Transformation | What filters, joins, classifications or derivations are required? | | Timing | What reference date, cut-off, frequency and history apply? | | Controls | What validations, reconciliations and evidence are required? | | Acceptance | What observable result proves the requirement is satisfied? | Acceptance criteria should state the expected outcome, not merely "UAT successful". A requirement for a counterparty country field might specify the governed definition, source authority, applicable code set, null treatment and reconciliation expectation. ### Where it sits ### Ownership | Role | Delivery responsibility | | :--- | :--- | | BA / requirements lead | Elicits, resolves and documents testable need | | Data owner | Approves governed meaning and material requirements | | Producer / technology | Confirms implementability and source constraints | | Consumer | Confirms the requirement supports intended use | | Challenge / control | Tests whether control obligations are captured | ### Permanent rule If a requirement cannot be objectively tested, it is not yet sufficiently specified for controlled delivery. ### Permanent trap Copying a regulatory label into a BRD and treating it as a definition. Regulatory terms still need scope, grain, source interpretation and handling rules before implementation. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** The BA method is universal; the underlying regulatory requirement can differ by jurisdiction.

title: Source Discovery and ETL Sourcing Analysis
one_screen: Source discovery is the analysis required before a mapping can be trusted. The BA or data analyst identifies candidate sources, determines their grain, keys, history, authority, refresh, embedded transformations and quality limitations, then documents why the selected path is appropriate for the requirement.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Sourcing question | Defect prevented | | :--- | :--- | | Is this source authoritative for the concept? | Choosing a convenient downstream copy over the governed source | | What is the row grain? | Duplicate joins and accidental aggregation | | Which key links to other datasets? | Orphan records and many-to-many multiplication | | What history is retained? | Inability to reproduce prior reporting dates | | Is the field raw or already transformed? | Applying the same business rule twice | | When is it available? | Missing reporting cut-off or using stale data | | What known defects exist? | Building a new report on an uncontrolled weakness | ETL sourcing analysis is not code design. It establishes the business and data facts that developers need before implementing extraction and transformation logic. ### Where it sits ### Never confuse [Source discovery] and [Source selection] **Source discovery** - investigates all plausible sources and their characteristics. --- **Source selection** - the governed decision on which path satisfies the requirement. Selection without discovery can institutionalise the first convenient answer. ### Permanent rule The chosen source path must be explainable in terms of authority, grain, timing, history and quality, not personal familiarity with a system. ### Permanent trap Beginning the mapping with target columns and asking developers where they can find something similar. Similar field names are weak evidence of equivalent business meaning. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** Source analysis is a delivery practice independent of the reporting jurisdiction.

title: Source-to-Target Mapping Specification
one_screen: A source-to-target mapping specification is the field-level implementation contract between a governed source and a target dataset, report or return. It must make joins, filters, transformations, classifications, defaults and lineage explicit enough that development and testing can independently reproduce the intended result.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Mapping column | What it must establish | | :--- | :--- | | Requirement ID | Why the target field exists and which approved need it satisfies | | Target field | Name, definition, datatype, grain and mandatory status | | Source | System, object, field and authoritative-source status | | Join / key | How source records connect without duplication or loss | | Filter | Which records enter or leave the target population | | Transformation | Derivation, aggregation, sign, unit, date or currency treatment | | Reference mapping | Governed code conversion and version | | Null / default logic | What happens when source data is absent or invalid | | Control | Validation or reconciliation that proves implementation | | Version | Effective date and approved change history | A mapping should avoid hidden logic such as "standard treatment" unless that treatment is separately controlled and versioned. If logic depends on a lookup table, the lookup source and effective version belong in the specification. ### Where it sits ### Never confuse [Mapping rule] and [Business definition] **Mapping rule** - how a defined concept is implemented from source fields into a target. --- **Business definition** - what the concept means. A technically perfect mapping to the wrong definition is still wrong. ### Permanent rule Every target field that matters must be traceable to an approved requirement and governed source logic, including handling of missing and exceptional cases. ### Permanent trap Documenting only Source Field -> Target Field. Most material reporting defects live in the omitted joins, filters, transformations, reference mappings and defaults. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** Mapping practice is universal; target templates and taxonomies differ by jurisdiction.

title: Test Strategy and Test Packs
one_screen: Testing proves that approved requirements and mappings have been implemented, not merely that code executes without error. A test strategy defines what must be proven across the data chain; a test pack turns that strategy into traceable scenarios, inputs, expected outcomes and retained evidence.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Test layer | What it proves | Typical evidence | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Field logic | Transformation implements the mapping | Known input -> expected target value | | Population | Inclusion and exclusion rules work | In-scope and out-of-scope records | | Boundary | Thresholds, dates and edge conditions behave correctly | Values immediately around cut-offs | | Negative | Invalid or missing data is controlled | Rejection, exception or governed default | | Reconciliation | Aggregates and populations remain complete | Source-to-target counts and balances | | Regression | Existing behaviour not intended to change still works | Prior scenarios rerun after change | Expected results should be calculated independently where practical. Repeating the developer's transformation in the test script can reproduce the same logic error and create false assurance. ### Where it sits ### Ownership | Role | Test responsibility | | :--- | :--- | | BA / test analyst | Designs scenarios from requirements and mappings | | Developer | Performs technical testing and fixes defects | | Business consumer | Confirms business scenarios and expected outcomes | | Data owner | Ensures material CDE and control coverage | | Challenge / control | Reviews adequacy where independent assurance is required | ### Permanent rule Test coverage follows the risk of being wrong, not the number of fields changed. ### Permanent trap Testing only happy-path records. Reporting defects frequently occur at nulls, effective-date boundaries, joins, duplicated keys, unusual classifications and exception handling. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** The testing method is universal; jurisdiction-specific rules simply create different scenarios and expected outcomes.

title: UAT Coverage and Business Evidence
one_screen: User Acceptance Testing, or UAT, is the business decision that the delivered data behaviour satisfies the approved need in realistic use. It is not a duplicate of developer testing: UAT focuses on end-to-end business scenarios, definitions, usability, exceptions and evidence that the consumer can rely on the output.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | UAT control | Question | | :--- | :--- | | Requirement coverage | Has every material requirement been exercised or explicitly dispositioned? | | Scenario realism | Do cases reflect real products, populations and reporting conditions? | | Expected outcome | Is the pass result known before execution? | | Evidence | Can another reviewer reproduce what was tested and observed? | | Defect linkage | Are failures tied to requirements, mappings and impacted reports? | | Acceptance | Are residual limitations understood and approved by the right authority? | UAT should include consumers who understand the reporting or risk use. A technically correct field can still fail because the wrong definition was agreed, required history is absent or a downstream user cannot distinguish a legitimate null from missing data. ### Where it sits ### Never confuse [UAT] and [System testing] **UAT** - asks whether the solution satisfies the approved business need and can be relied on in use. --- **System testing** - asks whether the technical solution behaves according to specifications. Both are necessary when business meaning and technical implementation can diverge. ### Permanent rule UAT sign-off is evidence of acceptance against defined criteria, not a ceremonial approval after a deadline has already forced go-live. ### Permanent trap Using only production-like totals as UAT evidence. Aggregate agreement can hide wrong classifications, duplicated records or incorrect edge-case treatment. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** UAT practice is universal; the scenarios inherit jurisdiction-specific reporting requirements where relevant.

title: Downstream Extract Validation
one_screen: A change can be correct in the warehouse and still be wrong in the file actually consumed or submitted. Downstream extract validation proves that the final population, fields, totals, formats and cut-off survive every post-mapping transformation, aggregation and packaging step.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Validation | What it catches | | :--- | :--- | | Record count / population | Dropped or duplicated rows | | Key-field comparison | Incorrect identifiers or classifications | | Aggregate reconciliation | Sign, unit or aggregation errors | | Reference-date check | Wrong reporting cut-off or stale load | | Format / schema check | Invalid datatype, length, enumeration or file structure | | Control-total check | Truncation or packaging failure after upstream testing | The final extract is a separate control point because downstream scripts, reporting tools and submission converters can contain logic not represented in the main ETL mapping. Validation should therefore compare back to governed upstream checkpoints rather than trusting that an earlier successful test remains valid after packaging. ### Where it sits ### Never confuse [Extract validation] and [Schema validation] **Extract validation** - proves the content is the right population and values for the intended use. --- **Schema validation** - proves the file conforms technically to a required structure. A perfectly valid file can contain the wrong numbers. ### Permanent rule The artifact that leaves the bank or feeds the final report must be validated as an artifact in its own right. ### Permanent trap Reconciling before the final reporting layer and assuming nothing can change afterwards. Late transformations, sign conventions, formatting or filters can introduce defects after upstream controls have passed. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** The validation mechanic is universal; technical schemas and submission formats vary by reporting estate.

title: Defect Tracking, Retest and Closure
one_screen: Delivery defects need a controlled lifecycle separate from long-term enterprise data issues, while material defects can escalate into that issue framework. A defect record links observed failure to requirement, mapping, severity, fix, retest and regression evidence so release decisions are based on known residual risk.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Defect field | Why it matters | | :--- | :--- | | Observed vs expected | States the failure objectively | | Requirement / mapping link | Identifies intended behaviour | | Severity and impact | Determines release and escalation consequence | | Root cause | Distinguishes requirement, data, code or environment failure | | Fix version | Identifies what changed | | Retest evidence | Proves the original failure is removed | | Regression impact | Proves the fix did not break adjacent logic | | Closure authority | Prevents self-declared completion | Severity is based on impact, not development effort. A one-line mapping error can be critical if it contaminates a regulatory population; a complex cosmetic defect may be low severity. ### Where it sits ### Never confuse [Defect] and [Data issue] **Defect** - a failure of delivered behaviour against an approved requirement or expected result during change delivery. --- **Data issue** - a broader governed weakness in live enterprise data or controls. A defect can reveal or become a data issue when the cause extends beyond the change. ### Permanent rule A fix is not closed until the failed scenario passes and the relevant regression scope remains sound. ### Permanent trap Closing a defect because the developer cannot reproduce it. The correct next step is evidence-based triage of data, environment and scenario conditions, not deletion of the problem. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** Defect mechanics are delivery controls and do not change by jurisdiction.

title: Regulatory Returns Production Cycle
one_screen: A regulatory return is produced through a controlled recurring cycle, not a one-off query at filing time. The cycle freezes the applicable requirement and reference date, sources the governed population, transforms it into return fields, validates and reconciles the output, resolves exceptions and creates a submission-ready artifact with retained evidence.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Production control | Evidence | | :--- | :--- | | Version control | Applicable instructions, form or taxonomy at the reference date | | Completeness | Population counts and source coverage | | Transformation | Approved mappings and job versions | | Reconciliation | Source-to-return and risk-to-finance controls where relevant | | Adjustments | Reason, owner, approver and reversal or remediation path | | Exceptions | Impact assessment and disposition | | Review | Named preparer / checker or equivalent control | PD, LGD, EAD, RWA, ECL staging, LCR and NSFR may feed returns, but their calculation mechanics belong to CR, CAP, IMP and TLM. DAT owns whether the resulting data reaches the return accurately and traceably. ### Where it sits ### Permanent rule Every submitted field should be reproducible for its reference date from governed source data, approved transformation logic and retained control evidence. ### Permanent trap Using the prior-period return as the primary source for the current return. Prior returns are useful for analytical comparison, not as a substitute for rebuilding from governed current-period data. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta in the production logic.** The forms, taxonomies, deadlines, validation rules and submission channels differ and are owned by the jurisdiction atoms.

title: Submission, Attestation and Restatement
one_screen: Submission is the control boundary where a production-ready return becomes an official filing. Attestation or authorised sign-off establishes accountable approval where the applicable regime requires it; if a material error is discovered afterwards, the bank must assess the affected filing, follow the regulator's correction process and preserve a clear restatement trail.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Control point | Minimum evidence | | :--- | :--- | | Approval | Who approved, what version, when | | Transmission | Submitted file or form and technical identifier | | Receipt | Portal acknowledgement or equivalent evidence | | Correction | Original vs corrected values and reason | | Impact | Affected returns, periods and linked decisions | | Remediation | Root cause, issue owner and permanent fix | Attestation is not assumed to have one universal signatory. The required certification, maker-checker structure and correction mechanics depend on the specific return and jurisdiction. ### Where it sits ### Never confuse [Attestation] and [Independent assurance] **Attestation** - accountable management certification or approval required by the applicable filing process. --- **Independent assurance** - separate review or audit that tests evidence. Management sign-off does not become independent because it is formal. ### Permanent rule A correction does not erase the original filing history; the bank must preserve what was submitted, what changed, why and who approved the correction. ### Jurisdiction variants #### EU (EBA / competent authority) Submission and correction mechanics follow the applicable supervisory reporting framework, national competent authority channel and taxonomy validations; there is no single universal EBA executive attestor for every return. #### UK (PRA) PRA data items and submission processes apply through the UK reporting estate; approval responsibilities are determined by the relevant return and firm's governance. #### US Call Reports and Federal Reserve reports have form-specific signature, certification and amendment instructions. These requirements must be read from the applicable form family rather than generalised across all US filings. #### IN (RBI) RBI supervisory returns are submitted through designated online portals under applicable directions and return instructions; maker-checker access and correction controls are governed by the relevant portal and return framework.

title: EU COREP/FINREP and UK PRA Reporting
one_screen: EU and UK prudential reporting share historical roots but are now separate estates. EU institutions use EBA supervisory frameworks such as COREP and FINREP with the EBA Data Point Model and taxonomies; PRA firms use applicable UK data items and Bank of England taxonomies.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Dimension | EU | UK | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Prudential reporting owner | EU legal framework with EBA technical standards | PRA Rulebook and PRA policy | | Core reporting families | COREP for prudential data; FINREP for supervisory financial reporting where applicable | PRA data items, including UK implementations and retained / restated reporting requirements | | Technical model | EBA DPM, validation rules and XBRL taxonomy packages | Bank of England Banking XBRL taxonomy and PRA instructions | | Change control | EBA reporting framework releases and EU legal adoption | PRA policy statements plus Bank of England taxonomy releases | As at August 2026, **EBA/CP/2026/07**, dated 10 April 2026, is a closed consultation, not a final rule: the general consultation closed 10 July 2026, with an earlier 10 May 2026 deadline for specified IFRS 18-related FINREP items. EBA Reporting Framework 4.4 applies by module with future first-reference dates; its July 2026 technical package was still draft ahead of final publication planned for September 2026. For the UK, **PS1/26**, published 20 January 2026, is final policy, not a consultation. Its Basel 3.1 reporting requirements take effect from 1 January 2027. Bank of England Banking XBRL taxonomy **v4.1.1**, published 27 August 2026, is a corrective release implementing policy intended to take effect from 1 January 2027; it is future-effective as at August 2026. ### Where it sits ### Permanent rule Use the framework and taxonomy applicable to the reporting reference date; current publication date and effective reporting date are not the same thing. ### Jurisdiction variants #### EU (EBA) COREP and FINREP sit in the EBA supervisory reporting architecture. EBA/CP/2026/07 remains a closed consultation as at August 2026; draft or future framework content must not be taught as already effective. #### UK (PRA) The UK has its own PRA reporting and Bank of England taxonomy estate. PS1/26 is final, while its relevant Basel 3.1 reporting changes and taxonomy v4.1.1 are future-effective from 1 January 2027.

title: US Regulatory Reports
one_screen: US prudential reporting is organised around named form families with respondent panels and form-specific instructions rather than one COREP-style taxonomy estate. The bank must determine form applicability from institution profile and current instructions, then preserve mappings to each required schedule.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Form | Who files it | What it covers | Cadence | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | FFIEC 031 | Banks with domestic and foreign offices | Call Report: condition, income and supporting schedules | Quarterly | | FFIEC 041 | Banks with domestic offices only that do not use FFIEC 051 | Call Report: condition, income and supporting schedules | Quarterly | | FFIEC 051 | Eligible banks with domestic offices only and total assets below the form's threshold; current FFIEC description states less than USD 5 billion | Streamlined Call Report: condition, income and supporting schedules | Quarterly | | FR Y-9C | BHCs, SLHCs, IHCs and SHCs meeting the respondent criteria; current page states generally USD 3 billion or more, subject to specified exceptions | Consolidated financial statements for holding companies | Quarterly | | FR Y-14A | Covered large firms in the FR Y-14 panel | Capital-assessment and stress-testing projections | Annual | | FR Y-14Q | Covered large firms in the FR Y-14 panel | Detailed asset, capital and PPNR data, with schedule-specific exceptions | Quarterly | | FR Y-14M | Applicable firms in the FR Y-14 panel with relevant portfolios | Detailed retail loan portfolio data | Monthly | As at August 2026, FFIEC 031/041/051 current materials include June 2026 forms or instructions. ### Where it sits ### Never confuse [US form family] and [Taxonomy-driven reporting framework] **US form family** - a named collection with defined respondent panel, schedules and instructions; applicability is determined form by form. --- **Taxonomy-driven reporting framework** - a broader technical reporting model where templates and data points are released through a common taxonomy architecture. The EU example is closer to this model. ### Permanent rule Never infer US filing obligations from a bank label alone; use the current respondent panel and instructions for the specific form and reference date. ### Jurisdiction variants #### US (FFIEC / Federal Reserve) The real delta is form selection, respondent panel and cadence. FFIEC Call Reports, FR Y-9C and FR Y-14 serve different entities and supervisory purposes and should not be treated as interchangeable versions of one return.

title: RBI Returns, ADF and CIMS
one_screen: India's supervisory reporting architecture combines return-specific RBI directions, the Automated Data Flow discipline and CIMS as a major filing platform. The durable objective is governed system-to-regulator flow with defined sources, reconciliation and increasing automation, while RBI's SDMX element-based programme remains an evolving architecture as at August 2026.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Layer | Owns | | :--- | :--- | | Supervisory-return directions | Applicability, governance, filing requirements, timelines and portals | | ADF | Controlled, increasingly automated sourcing from bank systems into RBI reporting | | CIMS | RBI online platform for return submission, data dissemination and related processes | | SDMX element-based programme | Phase-wise move toward standardised element-level collection | The regulatory baseline changed in 2026. The **Master Direction - Reserve Bank of India (Filing of Supervisory Returns) Directions - 2024**, RBI/DoS.DSG/2023-24/110 and DoS.DSG.No.10/33.01.001/2023-24, dated 27 February 2024, consolidated then-applicable instructions across several supervised-entity classes. For commercial banks, **Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Supervisory Returns) Directions, 2026**, RBI/DoS/2026-27/415 and DoS.CO.DSG.9/33.01.001/2026-27, was issued 31 July 2026 and took immediate effect. It addresses governance, data architecture, reconciliation, source records, automation and online filing. ADF predates CIMS. RBI's 27 September 2011 FAQ describes correct and consistent data through automated flow; CIMS is a later platform layer. As at August 2026, SDMX element-based reporting is **not complete**. RBI's Annual Report 2024-25 records application development, select-return testing and a pilot, with phase-wise rollout as the next step. ### Where it sits ### Never confuse [ADF] and [CIMS] **ADF** - the discipline of controlled, increasingly automated flow from bank systems into regulatory reporting. --- **CIMS** - an RBI platform for return submission, dissemination and related purposes. Portal use alone does not prove the upstream flow is automated or well governed. ### Permanent rule Portal submission is the end of the reporting chain, not evidence that upstream data architecture, reconciliation and automation are adequate. ### Jurisdiction variants #### IN (RBI) As at August 2026, commercial banks are governed by the 31 July 2026 Commercial Banks - Supervisory Returns Directions. The 2024 Master Direction is the predecessor consolidation; SDMX element-based reporting remains a phase-wise programme, not a completed universal replacement of return-based reporting.

title: Bank as a Balance Sheet
one_screen: A bank is first an accounting entity with resources, obligations, and a residual claim. The identity **Assets = Liabilities + Equity** is the frame through which every later banking concept—lending, deposits, profit, capital, liquidity, and loss—must be read.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Element | Meaning on the bank's balance sheet | Typical bank items | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Assets | Economic resources or claims controlled by the bank | Cash, central-bank balances, securities, loans | | Liabilities | Present obligations of the bank | Customer deposits, wholesale borrowings, payables | | Equity | Residual after liabilities are deducted from assets | Share capital, retained earnings, reserves | A customer's loan is normally a **bank asset** because the customer owes the bank. A customer's deposit is normally a **bank liability** because the bank owes the customer. The label follows the reporting entity's perspective, not everyday language. ### Formula ### Flow ### Where it sits ### Permanent rule Read every item from the reporting bank's perspective. A customer's asset can be the bank's liability, and a customer's liability can be the bank's asset. ### Never confuse [Equity] and [Cash] **Equity** — the residual interest after liabilities are deducted from assets. --- **Cash** — an asset available for payment; a bank can have substantial equity without holding the same amount as cash. ### Permanent trap Treating a customer's deposit as a bank asset because the money is “at the bank”. The deposit is a claim the customer has against the bank, so it is normally the bank's liability. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** The balance-sheet identity and reporting-entity perspective do not change by banking regulator or jurisdiction.

title: Deposits, Loans and Funding
one_screen: Deposits and loans are easiest to understand as opposite claims viewed from opposite sides of the same contracts. Deposits are normally bank liabilities, loans made by the bank are normally bank assets, and **funding** describes the liabilities and equity that support the asset side over time.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Contract | Customer view | Bank view | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Positive deposit balance | Asset: claim on bank | Liability: amount owed to customer | | Loan made by bank | Liability: amount owed to bank | Asset: claim on borrower | Funding answers a different question from classification: **what supports the bank's assets?** Customer deposits are one source; wholesale borrowing and equity are others. No rule says each unit of deposit funding must be traceable to a particular loan. A bank therefore has two simultaneous relationships with many customers: it can owe them deposits while other customers owe it loans. The balance sheet aggregates these positions rather than pairing each depositor with each borrower. ### Flow ### Where it sits ### Permanent rule Instrument classification follows the reporting entity's rights and obligations; funding describes how the asset side is supported, not where a specific currency unit “came from”. ### Never confuse [Deposit] and [Bank asset] **Deposit** — normally a liability of the bank because the bank owes the depositor. --- **Bank asset** — a resource or claim controlled by the bank, such as cash, securities, or a loan receivable. ### Never confuse [Funding] and [Cash] **Funding** — liabilities and equity supporting assets. --- **Cash** — one asset on the balance sheet; receiving funding can increase cash, but the concepts are not the same. ### Permanent trap Saying “deposits are money in the bank, therefore deposits are bank assets”. That description uses the customer's intuition while reading the bank's balance sheet. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** The contractual perspective and the distinction between funding sources and assets are universal mechanics.

title: How Bank Lending Creates Deposits
one_screen: When a bank originates a loan and credits the borrower's account, it can create a loan asset and a deposit liability at the same moment. “Loans create deposits” describes that balance-sheet mechanism; it does **not** mean lending is unconstrained by funding, settlement liquidity, capital, risk, or profitability.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism Suppose the bank grants a new loan of 100 and credits the proceeds to the borrower's deposit account: | Bank entry | Change | | :--- | ---: | | Loan asset | +100 | | Deposit liability | +100 | | Total assets | +100 | | Total liabilities | +100 | | Equity at origination, before fees/costs | No mechanical change | The key next step is payment. If the borrower pays someone who banks elsewhere, the newly created deposit can leave the originating bank. Interbank settlement then requires the originating bank to transfer settlement assets, normally central-bank money within the relevant payment system. The bank must manage the liquidity and funding position left behind. ### Flow ### Where it sits ### Permanent rule Creating a deposit at loan origination and funding the resulting balance sheet are compatible truths, not competing theories. ### Never confuse [Deposit creation] and [Funding] **Deposit creation** — the simultaneous increase in a loan asset and deposit liability when lending is booked in this form. --- **Funding** — the liabilities and equity that support assets over time, including after customers transfer newly created deposits elsewhere. ### Permanent trap Turning “banks create deposits by lending” into “banks can lend without constraint”. A bank that cannot settle payments, fund its assets, absorb losses, satisfy constraints, or earn an adequate return cannot sustainably expand lending. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** The double-entry mechanism is universal. Payment-system design and prudential calibration differ, but those differences do not alter the accounting logic.

title: The Bank Earnings Engine
one_screen: A traditional bank earns interest on many assets and pays interest on much of its funding. **Net interest income (NII) = interest income − interest expense**; profit then reflects non-interest income, operating costs, credit-loss charges, market or valuation effects where applicable, and tax.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Layer | What moves it | | :--- | :--- | | Interest income | Asset balances · contractual/effective yields · repricing · collection | | Interest expense | Deposit and borrowing balances · funding mix · repricing | | Net interest income | Interest income minus interest expense | | Pre-provision operating result | NII plus non-interest income minus operating costs | | Profit | Further accounting gains/losses · credit-loss charges · tax and other items | A bank can therefore grow NII while profit falls if expenses or credit-loss charges rise faster. Equally, a bank can report strong profit despite weak NII if non-interest income is unusually high. ### Formula ### Flow ### Where it sits ### Permanent rule Profit is broader than spread income. A bank's earnings must be read through both the quantity of business and the prices, costs, losses, and timing attached to it. ### Never confuse [Net interest income] and [Net interest margin] **Net interest income** — an amount of income. --- **Net interest margin** — a ratio scaling NII to average earning assets. ### Permanent trap Calling the difference between a headline loan rate and a headline deposit rate “the bank's NIM”. Balances differ, funding is broader than deposits, instruments reprice at different times, and NIM has an asset denominator. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.** Presentation conventions differ, but the economic distinction between interest income, interest expense, NII, and a margin ratio is universal.

title: Capital, Liquidity and Solvency
one_screen: Capital, liquidity, and solvency answer different questions. **Capital absorbs losses; liquidity enables payments when due; solvency concerns whether the value of assets is sufficient relative to obligations.** Confusing them hides the two distinct ways a bank can fail: loss of value and loss of payment capacity.
bodyText: ### Core mechanism | Question | Concept | Failure mode | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Can losses be absorbed? | Capital | Losses exhaust loss-absorbing resources | | Can obligations be paid on time? | Liquidity | Usable cash/settlement resources are insufficient when needed | | Are assets worth enough relative to obligations? | Solvency | Economic asset value falls below obligations | Accounting equity and regulatory capital are related but not identical. Prudential frameworks apply eligibility criteria, deductions, and adjustments when deciding what counts as regulatory capital. A solvent bank can still be illiquid: it may own valuable long-dated assets but lack immediately usable settlement resources.
